setlist.title: I've Been All Around This World

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Hard To Handle** (1 review): Reviewer ranks this among the best 1970 versions, with notable intensity from Garcia [8]
- **Saw Mill** (1 review): Saw Mill is one of several rarely played songs on this recording [4]
- **Katie Mae** (1 review): Reviewer calls Katie Mae an especially strong blues performance [11]

## Setlist highlights

- **Long Black Limousine**: rare: 4 archived performances [15]
- **Seasons Of My Heart**: earliest performance in the archive; rare: 6 archived performances [15]
- **Saw Mill**: earliest performance in the archive; rare: 6 archived performances [15]
- **Bound In Memories**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [15]
- **Little Sadie**: rare: 7 archived performances [15]
- **Katie Mae**: earliest performance in the archive; rare: 10 archived performances [15]

## The recordings

- **gd70-01-31.sbd.cotsman.7045.sbefail.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 18 songs; 96 min; rated 4.1/5 by 20 [1]. Said about its sound: Some tape hiss is audible, but the recording is acceptable [4]
- **gd1970-01-31.sbd.cotsman.fixed.24028.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 18 songs; 96 min; rated 3.62/5 by 8 [2]

## Around the show

- Reviewer believes this was the show where Pigpen returned to organ, though unsure [6]
- Phil's amp trouble led to an unplanned second set that some think worked better than planning [7]
- Reviewer hears a band that seems irritated to be there; Phil's bass amp then fails [10]
- Phil's amp failed, forcing an unscheduled acoustic set to close the show [1]
- Garcia played electric guitar during part of the acoustic set [1]
- The band was busted by New Orleans police before the show, prompting stage banter [1]
- Phil's amp failed, so an unplanned acoustic set closed the show [2]
- The band was arrested by New Orleans police before the show, which fed the stage banter [2]
- Reviewer finds the electric set average for 1970, with the acoustic set the highlight [9]
- Songs are short, album-length, lacking the extended jamming typical of the era [10]
- Reviewer says the material sounds like what should have been a follow-up album to Workingman's Dead [14]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd70-01-31.sbd.cotsman.7045.sbefail.shnf**: transferred by Paul Hartman and JCotsman; source: Soundboard [1]
- **gd1970-01-31.sbd.cotsman.fixed.24028.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Jeff Cotsman; source: SBD>MR>C>D>CD>EAC>SHN [2]. Also: Recording was normalized in Sound Forge, pops removed, and Shntool fixed sector boundary errors [2]
